title.narrative: Modernization of Public Financial Management Systems Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Modernization of Public Financial Management (PFM) Systems Project for Iraq is to improve financial information management and transparency, cash management, public investment management, and public procurement modernization at selected federal and governorate agencies. The first component is PFM. It consists of following sub-components: (i) integrated financial management information system (IFMIS) design and initial implementation; (ii) PFM capacity development; (iii) internal audit modernization at the Federal Ministry of Finance; (iv) PFM systems at the subnational level; and (v) project management and reform coordination. The second component is public investment management and public procurement at the Federal level. It consists of following sub-components: (i) public investment management system (PIMS) strengthening; (ii) public procurement modernization; and (iii) project management and reform coordination. The third component is public investment management and public procurement at the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) level. It consists of following sub-components: (i) PIMS strengthening; (ii) public procurement modernization; and (iii) project management and reform coordination.
The project development objective (PDO) is to improve budget transparency at the federal level and public investment management and public procurement at the Kurdistan Regional Government level.

title.narrative: Share of federal budget executed through the TSA (Percentage)

comment.narrative: A workshop was conducted in Amman/Jordan during June 13-15, 2023, with support from both the IMF's Middle East Regional Technical Assistance Center (METAC) and the World Bank. Strengthening cash management with a well-functioning TSA is a foundation for Iraq's Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms and preparations for the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). At a minimum, the TSA should cover all budgetary central government entities and their transactions; include all central government bank accounts; and provide the option to also include foreign currency denominated accounts, including loans from the multilateral institutions, and donor aid resources. Donors should be encouraged to integrate their funds with the TSA or, as a minimum, to route final payments through the TSA. A draft road map for TSA implementation was prepared at the workshop.

title.narrative: Citizen's budgets posted on the MoF website

comment.narrative: The Federal Ministry prepared the country's first citizen's budget document for 2018. Draft Citizen Budget was prepared for 2019, however, it was not finalized and published due to challenges of the 2019 budget preparation process. A draft Citizen Budget for 2020 was prepared but the Annual Public Budget Law was not enacted by the Parliament. Thereafter, Citizen Budget is not being produced.

title.narrative: Use of KRG e-GP system for public tenders and contract awards for goods and small works . (Percentage by number of tenders and contracts)

comment.narrative: Only five each goods and small works tenders were advertised on the e-GP pilot system (http://keps.digital.gov.krd/). Discussions with the Ministry of Planning showed that the system was not ready for implementation due to many shortcomings such as the need to build capacity for both the public and private sectors to deal with the system.

title.narrative: Share of public investment projects (per threshold) in pilot line ministries at the KRG level that are subject to new appraisal and selection mechanisms and registered in the KDMS (Percent )

comment.narrative: Public investment projects are registered in the Kurdistan Development Management System (KDMS). The KDMS includes investment projects for the 3 pilot line ministries (Health, Education, and Agriculture) covering all ongoing and completed projects that started in 2022. However, the projects were included in the budget and then later in the KDMS without subjection to the new appraisal and selection mechanisms.

comment.narrative:
Annual financial statements compliant with IPSAS are not being prepared; 2009 is the latest final account - http://mof.gov.iq/pages/ar/PublicFunndss.aspx
Citizen Feedback mechanism is not available.

The Bank issued ‘no objection on February 27, 2023, for publication of the Special Procurement Notice (SPN) for Initial Selection for a “Turnkey Solution”. With the cancellation of funds allocated to IFMIS component, this indicator was no longer achievable.

title.narrative: Annual Budget prepared on new chart of accounts/budget classification using IFMIS

comment.narrative: The Middle East Regional Technical Assistance Center (METAC) provided technical assistance (TA) on new chart of accounts/budget classification. The TA defined a short-term action plan for the implementation of the new classification and chart of accounts considering the requirements of the IFMIS. With the cancellation of funds allocated to IFMIS component, this indicator was no longer achievable.

title.narrative: Use of SBDs prepared with new procurement regulations at the KRG level (Percentage by number of SBD's)

comment.narrative: Nine (9) Standard Bidding Documents (SBDs) were developed. From the SBDs developed, only one (framework agreement for health) was not used due to not issuing activities needed to use this document, while all other documents have been used.
